newsitem.title: USA: Grubb & Ellis sees gain from retiring debt.
newsitem.headline: Grubb & Ellis sees gain from retiring debt.

text.p: Grubb & Ellis Co said Thursday it expects an additional $2 million extraordinary gain on the early retirement of debt in its third quarter ending March 31.
The company recorded a similar gain in the second quarter, amounting to $3.6 million.

In explaining the expected gain, the real estate company said on January 27, 1997 that it sold 2.5 million shares of its common stock for $11.3 million to Archon Group LP, a majority owned subsidiary of Goldman, Sachs & Co.

Concurrently, Grubb & Ellis purchased from Warburg, Pincus and then retired $10 million of outstanding 9.9 percent senior notes and $5 million revolving credit note that Warburg, Pincus acquired from Prudential Insurance Co of America on October 22, 1996. It said the aggregate purchase price for the 9.9 percent notes and revolving credit note was $13 million plus accrued interest.

With this transaction, Grubb & Ellis currently has no remaining outstanding long-term debt. The company said it is in negotiations to secure a bank line of credit for general corporate purposes and acquisitions.
